Student of WarClassFighterAt 3rd level, you gain proficiency with one type of artisan’s tools of your choice. (Cook's Utensils)

NOMBRE:

TIPO DE ORIGEN:
ManeuversClassFighterPushing Attack When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to drive the target back. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and if the target is Large or smaller, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, you push the target up to 15 feet away from you. Maneuvers: Pushing Attack: (No Action) Trip Attack When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to knock the target down. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and if the target is Large or smaller, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, you knock the target prone. Maneuvers: Trip Attack: (No Action) Goading Attack When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to goad the target into attacking you. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and the target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target has disadvantage on all attack rolls against targets other than you until the end of your next turn. Maneuvers: Goading Attack: (No Action) Precision Attack When you make a weapon attack roll against a creature, you can expend one superiority die to add it to the roll. You can use this maneuver before or after making the attack roll, but before any effects of the attack are applied. Maneuvers: Precision Attack: (No Action) Riposte When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction and expend one superiority die to make a melee weapon attack against the creature. If you hit, you add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll. Maneuvers: Riposte: 1 Reaction

SentinelFeatFighter lvl 4You have mastered techniques to take advantage of every drop in any enemy's guard, gaining the following benefits: When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn. Creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you even if they take the Disengage action before leaving your reach. When a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you (and that target doesn't have this feat), you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the attacking creature.

LanguagesRacialHuman VariantYou can speak, read, and write Common and one extra language of your choice. Humans typically learn the languages of other peoples they deal with, including obscure dialects. They are fond of sprinkling their speech with words borrowed from other tongues: Orc curses, Elvish musical expressions, Dwarvish military phrases, and so on. (Undercommon)

Great Weapon MasterFeatFighter lvl 6You've learned to put the weight of a weapon to your advantage, letting its momentum empower your strikes. You gain the following benefits: On your turn, when you score a critical hit with a melee weapon or reduce a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action. Before you make a melee attack with a heavy weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

Know Your EnemyClassFighterStarting at 7th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own. Combat SuperiorityClassFighterWhen you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice. Maneuvers. You learn three maneuvers of your choice, which are detailed under “Maneuvers” below. Many maneuvers enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one maneuver per attack. You learn two additional maneuvers of your choice at 7th, 10th, and 15th level. Each time you learn new maneuvers, you can also replace one maneuver you know with a different one. Superiority Dice. You have four superiority dice, which are d8s. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain all of your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest. You gain another superiority die at 7th level and one more at 15th level. Saving Throws. Some of your maneuvers require your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver’s effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows: Maneuver save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)
≡

TIPO DE ORIGEN:
Extra AttackClassFighter lvl 5Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 11th level in this class and to four when you reach 20th level in this class.
≡
y
NOMBRE:
ORIGEN:
TIPO DE ORIGEN:
Polearm MasterFeatVariant Human lvl 1You gain the following benefits: When you take the Attack action and attack with only a glaive, halberd, quarterstaff, or spear, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the opposite end of the weapon. This attack uses the same ability modifier as the primary attack. The weapon’s damage die for this attack is a d4, and it deals bludgeoning damage. While you are wielding a glaive, halberd, pike, quarterstaff, or spear, other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they enter the reach you have with that weapon.
≡

NOMBRE:
ORIGEN:
TIPO DE ORIGEN:
Action SurgeClassFighterStarting at 2nd level, you can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.
≡

NOMBRE:

TIPO DE ORIGEN:
Second WindClassFighterYou have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.
≡
y
NOMBRE:
ORIGEN:
TIPO DE ORIGEN:
IndomitableClassFighter lvl 9Beginning at 9th level, you can reroll a saving throw that you fail. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can’t use this feature again until you finish a long rest. You can use this feature twice between long rests starting at 13th level and three times between long rests starting at 17th level.

condiciones

ocultado

Un ejército oculto es más difícil de atacar y obtiene una bonificación de circunstancia de +2 a sus tiradas de Maniobra. Los ataques contra él sufren una penalización de circunstancia de -2. Esta condición dura mientras persista el hecho que otorga el ocultamiento.

derrotado

Cuando un ejército tiene cero puntos de golpe, es derrotado. Un ejército derrotado no puede emprender acciones de guerra. Un ejército derrotado puede recuperarse hasta 1 punto de golpe con la actividad Recuperar ejército (aunque la CD básica aumenta en 5 para esta tirada). Cualquier efecto que restablezca a un ejército derrotado a al menos 1 punto de golpe, elimina la condición de derrota. Un ejército derrotado sólo puede moverse un hexágono a la vez con la actividad Desplegar ejército. Un ejército derrotado puede ser Disuelto normalmente. No puede usarse para ninguna otra actividad del Ejército mientras permanezca derrotado.\nSi un ejército derrotado sufre daño, debe superar una tirada básica de CD 16 o será destruido. Si todos los ejércitos de un bando son derrotados, esos ejércitos son destruidos.

destruido

El ejército ha quedado completamente devastado y no puede restaurarse; solo puede ser reemplazado por un nuevo ejército. Todo el equipo que tenía el ejército está estropeado.

eficiente

El ejército ha realizado una actividad del Ejército con tal velocidad que puede usarse para intentar una segunda actividad del Ejército inmediatamente, pero al hacerlo pierde la condición de eficiencia. La segunda actividad del Ejército sufre una penalización -5 en su prueba, y el resultado de esta segunda prueba de actividad del Ejército no puede otorgar la condición de eficiencia. Si el ejército no intenta una segunda actividad del Ejército, pierde la condición de eficiente y reduce en 1 el valor de una condición de su elección.

comprometido

Un ejército que está en combate cuerpo a cuerpo con uno o más ejércitos enemigos queda comprometido. Se debe comprometer un ejército para intentar realizar ataques cuerpo a cuerpo. Si un ejército está comprometido e intenta una maniobra de acción de guerra que haría que dejase de estarlo, provoca reacciones de cualquier ejército enemigo con el que estuviera comprometido.

fortificado

El ejército se encuentra en una posición defensiva como resultado de una actividad del Ejército de Guarnición. Mientras están fortificados, los ejércitos enemigos no pueden enfrentarse al ejército y el ejército no puede enfrentarse a los ejércitos enemigos. Un ejército fortificado obtiene una bonificación de +4 de elemento a su CA y a las tiradas de Moral realizadas para reagruparse. Un ejército fortificado que utiliza una acción de guerra de maniobra pierde inmediatamente su condición de fortificado.

perdido

Cuando falla el intento de un ejército de desplegarse en una nueva ubicación, este puede perderse. Un ejército perdido no puede realizar otra actividad que no sea Recuperarse, y eso sólo en un intento de eliminar la condición de perdido. Cuando un ejército se recupera de la condición perdida, el DJ decide cuál es la nueva ubicación del ejército (normalmente es un punto medio aproximado entre el punto de partida del ejército y su destino previsto).

atascado

El movimiento del ejército se ve gravemente afectado. Puede estar atascado en barro, nieve, sotobosque, escombros o terreno similar, obstaculizado por el transporte de cargas pesadas o por cualquier otro motivo. Atascado siempre tiene un valor. Un ejército atascado sufre una penalización de circunstancia en todas las maniobras igual a su valor de atascado y a las pruebas de Despliegue del Ejército. Si un ejército alguna vez tiene un valor de atascado de 4, este queda inmovilizado.

distante

Un ejército que tiene la condición de distante ha logrado retirarse a una distancia considerable de los ejércitos enemigos y está potencialmente preparado para escapar del campo de batalla. Los ejércitos pueden intentar ataques a distancia contra ejércitos distantes, pero reciben una penalización de -5 en ese ataque.

flanqueado

El ejército tiene enemigos que vienen desde muchas direcciones y debe dividir sus fuerzas para hacer frente a las amenazas de todos lados. El ejército sufre una penalización de circunstancia de -2 a su CA.

fijado

El ejército ya no puede moverse con libertad. Tiene la condición de flanqueado y no puede utilizar ninguna acción de guerra de maniobra. No se puede desplegar un ejército fijado.

huido

El ejército se retira, ya sea por compulsión mágica o simplemente por pérdida de moral. En su turno, un ejército derrotado debe utilizar la acción de guerra Retirada. Mientras está derrotado, el ejército sufre una penalización de circunstancia de -2 a las pruebas de Moral. Esta condición finaliza automáticamente una vez que se resuelve un encuentro de guerra, pero el ejército derrotado aumenta su valor de sacudida en 1 en este caso. Si todos los ejércitos de un lado de una batalla son derrotados simultáneamente, la batalla termina y el otro ejército sale victorioso.

aturdido

La moral del ejército ha comenzado a flaquear, ya sea por miedo ante un enemigo poderoso, por un efecto sobrenatural como la temible presencia de un dragón, o simplemente por el resultado de la mala suerte en el curso de la batalla. Aturdido siempre tiene un valor numérico. Las pruebas de Moral del ejército reciben una penalización de circunstancia igual a su valor de conmoción, y cada vez que el ejército sufre daño, debe superar una tirada básica de CD 11 o su valor de conmoción aumenta en 1. Un ejército que queda conmocionado 4 es automáticamente derrotado. Un ejército reduce el valor de esta condición en 1 cada turno del Reino que pasa durante el cual no intenta una actividad del Ejército ni participa en un encuentro de guerra.

cansado

El ejército está agotado. Cansado siempre tiene un valor numérico. Un ejército cansado sufre una penalización de circunstancia igual a su valor de cansancio en su CA, en sus pruebas de Maniobra y en sus pruebas de actividad del Ejército; se necesita el doble de penalización por esta circunstancia en las pruebas de Desplegar Ejército. Un ejército reduce el valor de esta condición en 1 cada turno del Reino que pasa durante el cual no intenta una actividad del Ejército ni participa en un encuentro de guerra.

RASGOS Y ATRIBUTOS

1010
≡
Student of WarAt 3rd level, you gain proficiency with one type of artisan’s tools of your choice. (Cook's Utensils)
≡
ManeuversPushing Attack When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to drive the target back. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and if the target is Large or smaller, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, you push the target up to 15 feet away from you. Maneuvers: Pushing Attack: (No Action) Trip Attack When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to knock the target down. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and if the target is Large or smaller, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, you knock the target prone. Maneuvers: Trip Attack: (No Action) Goading Attack When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to goad the target into attacking you. You add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll, and the target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target has disadvantage on all attack rolls against targets other than you until the end of your next turn. Maneuvers: Goading Attack: (No Action) Precision Attack When you make a weapon attack roll against a creature, you can expend one superiority die to add it to the roll. You can use this maneuver before or after making the attack roll, but before any effects of the attack are applied. Maneuvers: Precision Attack: (No Action) Riposte When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction and expend one superiority die to make a melee weapon attack against the creature. If you hit, you add the superiority die to the attack’s damage roll. Maneuvers: Riposte: 1 Reaction
≡
SentinelYou have mastered techniques to take advantage of every drop in any enemy's guard, gaining the following benefits: When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn. Creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you even if they take the Disengage action before leaving your reach. When a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you (and that target doesn't have this feat), you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the attacking creature.
≡
LanguagesYou can speak, read, and write Common and one extra language of your choice. Humans typically learn the languages of other peoples they deal with, including obscure dialects. They are fond of sprinkling their speech with words borrowed from other tongues: Orc curses, Elvish musical expressions, Dwarvish military phrases, and so on. (Undercommon)
≡
Great Weapon MasterYou've learned to put the weight of a weapon to your advantage, letting its momentum empower your strikes. You gain the following benefits: On your turn, when you score a critical hit with a melee weapon or reduce a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action. Before you make a melee attack with a heavy weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.
≡
Know Your EnemyStarting at 7th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own. The DM tells you if the creature is your equal, superior, or inferior in regard to two of the following characteristics of your choice: Strength score Dexterity score Constitution score Armor Class Current hit points Total class levels (if any) Fighter class levels (if any) Know Your Enemy: (No Action)
≡
Ability Score Increase+2 strength score
≡
Fighting Style (Defense)While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.
≡
Ability Score IncreaseTwo different ability scores of your choice increase by 1. Strength Score Constitution Score
≡
SkillsYou gain proficiency in one skill of your choice. Athletics Choose two skills from Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Athletics, History, Insight, Intimidation, Perception, and Survival (Fighter) Perception Insight
≡
Combat SuperiorityWhen you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice. Maneuvers. You learn three maneuvers of your choice, which are detailed under “Maneuvers” below. Many maneuvers enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one maneuver per attack. You learn two additional maneuvers of your choice at 7th, 10th, and 15th level. Each time you learn new maneuvers, you can also replace one maneuver you know with a different one. Superiority Dice. You have four superiority dice, which are d8s. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain all of your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest. You gain another superiority die at 7th level and one more at 15th level. Saving Throws. Some of your maneuvers require your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver’s effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows: Maneuver save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice)
≡
Extra AttackBeginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 11th level in this class and to four when you reach 20th level in this class.
≡
Polearm MasterYou gain the following benefits: When you take the Attack action and attack with only a glaive, halberd, quarterstaff, or spear, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the opposite end of the weapon. This attack uses the same ability modifier as the primary attack. The weapon’s damage die for this attack is a d4, and it deals bludgeoning damage. While you are wielding a glaive, halberd, pike, quarterstaff, or spear, other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they enter the reach you have with that weapon.
≡
Action SurgeStarting at 2nd level, you can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.
≡
Second WindYou have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.
≡
IndomitableBeginning at 9th level, you can reroll a saving throw that you fail. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can’t use this feature again until you finish a long rest. You can use this feature twice between long rests starting at 13th level and three times between long rests starting at 17th level.
